questions.question: What does polymorphism mean?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows objects to take multiple forms.

questions.question: What polymorphism type is resolved at compile time?
What polymorphism type is resolved at runtime?
What technique creates multiple methods with same name?
questions.explanation: Overloading uses same name with different parameters.

questions.question: What technique redefines parent methods in child class?
What C++ keyword enables runtime polymorphism?
What distinguishes overloaded methods?
questions.explanation: Overloaded methods differ in parameter types or count.

questions.question: What binding occurs at compile time?
questions.explanation: Early binding resolves method calls before execution.

questions.question: What binding occurs at runtime?
questions.explanation: Late binding resolves method calls during execution.

questions.question: What typing checks behavior instead of type?
questions.explanation: Duck typing focuses on what objects can do.

questions.question: What is assigning a child object to a parent-type reference called?
questions.explanation: Upcasting is safe and implicit, e.g. Animal a = new Dog().

questions.question: What is converting a parent-type reference back to a child type called?
questions.explanation: Downcasting requires an explicit cast like (Dog) animal and can fail at runtime.

questions.question: Which Java keyword checks whether an object is of a given type at runtime?
questions.explanation: obj instanceof Type returns true when obj's runtime type matches.

questions.question: What must be identical between an overriding method and the parent method?
questions.explanation: An override must keep the same name and parameter list as the parent method.

questions.question: Which C# keyword marks a base class method as overridable?
questions.explanation: Virtual methods can be replaced in derived classes using override.
